Connect to foundations: Cosmic expansion and the Hubble–Lemaître law ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Label particles and move their positions Map initial Lagrangian labels q to later comoving positions x. The Zel’dovich approximation keeps the initial displacement direction and multiplies its amplitude by linear growth D. Physical position is r = ax, separating background expansion from peculiar displacement. x(q,t)=q+D(t)s(q), r=a(t)x This is first-order Lagrangian perturbation theory with growing-mode initial data, not an exact general orbit solution. It primarily describes pressureless matter before shell crossing. 02Density follows the volume Jacobian The mass of a labelled element is conserved. A small initial volume d³q maps to d³x = Jd³q; density therefore varies as the inverse determinant. J=det(δᵢⱼ+D∂sᵢ∂qⱼ), ρρ̄=1J For potential displacements, let λᵢ be eigenvalues of −∂sᵢ/∂qⱼ. Each direction has its own compression factor; the largest positive eigenvalue reaches collapse first. ρρ̄=1(1−Dλ₁)(1−Dλ₂)(1−Dλ₃) 03One collapsing direction gives a pancake Simultaneous collapse along three axes requires special symmetry. Compression along one direction first produces a sheet-like structure, hence the name pancake. s(q)=−Aksin(kq), x=q−DAksin(kq) J=1−DAcos(kq), ρρ̄=11−DAcos(kq) The periodic one-dimensional panel uses k = 1. It displays equally spaced particle labels and the density at their mapped Eulerian positions. Playback advances D uniformly, not cosmic time. 04Shell crossing ends the single-stream description At DA = 1 the first zero Jacobian forms a caustic. Collisionless matter can develop multiple streams; gas also needs pressure and shocks. Extending 1/J through negative Jacobians would give an unphysical negative density. Controls stop at DA ≤ 0.95. The panel does not compute post-collapse galaxies, shocks or published N-body results. Even as a peak grows, the mass in one period stays fixed. 05Connect geometry to halo statistics Zel’dovich approximates positions and shapes; Press–Schechter estimates halo statistics from smoothed fluctuations. A spherical-collapse threshold and anisotropic first shell crossing are different criteria. A specified displacement field extends the construction to multiple dimensions, while post-crossing evolution needs methods such as N-body dynamics. Identifying where the approximation fails is part of using it correctly. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. In the one-dimensional sinusoidal model, what is the peak density ratio at DA = 0.8? What fails at DA = 1? Show the answer and reasoning ρ/ρ̄ = 1/(1−DA) = 5, so δ = 4. At DA = 1 the map derivative vanishes and a caustic forms. Multiple streams can then occupy one location, invalidating a single-stream continuation; total particle mass does not become infinite.
